chapter: Brown's Band and Tom in Chicago
title: Tom with Ray Miller and Burt Kelly's Stables
summary: Tom played with Ray Miller's Memphis Melody Boys in a Chicago show and at Kelly's Stables, where Brown sat in briefly.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Didn't you have some piano roles or something you wanted to ask about?
I was going to ask a little bit about... If you remember any of the other bands that Tom played with, like Ray Miller, do you know anything about his activities with Ray Miller, for instance?

Yes, he was playing... He played with what they call the Memphis Melody Boys. Ray Miller had the Memphis Melody Boys in Edwin's production show. I caught the show when I was in Chicago. And Tom was... The whole band was pushed up on pedestals, way up high in the scenery of the show. It was quite a large show. And that was in 1920 that I heard Tom in that particular band. And he went back to New York with them. And later on, he come back to Chicago. And he played with Burt Kelly quite a lot. Burt Kelly Stables was well known all over Chicago. He played with Burt Kelly. Yeah, Burt Kelly Stables. Yes, I remember. He had a sort of an affair. He had these cafes built like a horse barn with stars in it. With harness and hay and everything else. And he'd tell the people as they came in, in their full dress suits and tuxedos and everything, there's your stall, get into it. You know? And it was really funny. They had hay all over and old pieces of harnesses decorating the place. And quite an outfit. And the 400 class got quite a kick out of it, you know? And he made quite a lot of money. He sold liquor and had shows, entertainment and things. Tom played there. And I, at one time, played with Tom's band in Chicago just for a little while. Would you like to see the picture of him?
Yeah, we'd like to see him after a while.
